title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
gist: Carl Benedikt Frey argues Europe's economic framework protects incumbent champions at the expense of future winners, and that Europe needs a new model promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale to stay competitive, sovereign and secure. He frames technology as a historical source of power, citing the westward shift of power after the Industrial Revolution.

insights.claim: Europe's economic framework protects yesterday's champions (incumbents) at the expense of tomorrow's potential winners, creating a dynamism deficit.
insights.speaker: CARL BENEDIKT FREY
insights.so_what: Implies structural drag on European innovation-led growth and a bias toward incumbent-heavy equity markets rather than scale-up winners.
insights.quote: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners.
insights.locator: Europe has built an economic framework

themes.theme: Prescription: innovation and commercialization at scale

insights.claim: To remain competitive, sovereign and secure in the 21st century, Europe needs a new economic model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.
insights.speaker: CARL BENEDIKT FREY
insights.so_what: Links European tech policy to sovereignty and security, suggesting policy pressure toward scale-up finance and industrial reform for European tech.
insights.quote: it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale
insights.locator: Europe has built an economic framework

themes.theme: Technology as a source of geopolitical power

insights.claim: Technology has historically been a source of power: when China sat near the frontier of invention it was also a master of statecraft, but Europe's Industrial Revolution technologies (steam, steel, railways, rifled artillery) shifted the balance of power westward.
insights.speaker: CARL BENEDIKT FREY
insights.so_what: Frames today's tech race as a determinant of the global balance of power, implying Europe's lag in frontier technology carries geopolitical, not just economic, costs.
insights.quote: Technology has always been a source of power.
insights.locator: OXFORD—Technology has always been a source

insights.claim: The Industrial Revolution's power shift inaugurated what China remembers as the 'century of humiliation', illustrating the long-run consequences of falling behind technologically.
insights.speaker: CARL BENEDIKT FREY
insights.so_what: Historical cautionary tale implying Europe risks a similar relative decline if it fails to close its innovation gap.
insights.locator: OXFORD—Technology has always been a source
